utterances.text: What happened to those who were incarcerated elsewhere, in the sports halls and elsewhere? Did they end up in Manjaca or were they released?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC
utterances.text: Either Manjaca or they were released, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I apologise. Please do not feel insulted by anything that I asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, thank you very much. There are a lot of documents that remain, but I can use them with some other witnesses. For me the most important things are the statements of these people, who are tendered into evidence and admitted into evidence in this case, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, I have a couple of questions for you. Very, very briefly, earlier this afternoon at page 106 of the transcript Mr. Karadzic put a question to you in relation to the Red Berets, which is mentioned in paragraph 51 of your statement, and he said you noticed the arrival of some Red Berets, and in paragraph 52 you say that you believe their intentions may have been good, and went further. You answered. You said: "Yes. They were billeted in the secretariat or the staff of Territorial Defence, and a certain number of those Green Berets were placed at the disposal of us in the police." Were you referring to Red Berets or Green Berets in your answer? Because "Green Berets" appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I misspoke. The word "green" should be replaced by the word "red." And I believe that it is obvious from the overall context of my responses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dzafic, thank you. I want to now -- I want you to look at two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could call up 65 ter number 00849A. And these two documents that I wish to show Mr. Dzafic have been faxed or e-mailed down to the Registrar in the Sarajevo field office.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Dzafic, this is a copy of a document, of 65 ter number 00849, that you saw this morning, which is behind tab number 13, which is now MFI P03490. We can see there that it has a Broj number, 05.01-118/1992. I would now like you to look at another --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 118/1992. I would now like you to look at another document, and this is 65 ter number 00848. And that is a document dated the same date, the 21st of July, 1992, with a Broj number, 05-01-117/1992. And it's dealing with the decision on the termination of employment of all employees who have filed respond to the general mobilisation. Is this consistent with your knowledge of what was going on in the Kljuc municipality in respect of mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC
utterances.text: The document under 117, and the last two numbers are /1992, is something I've never seen before, and this refers to the general mobilisation. As far as I can remember, I've not seen it before. In practice, the mobilisation was implemented in this exact way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were people's employment terminated who failed to respond to the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ATIF DZAFIC
utterances.text: I don't have any specific information about anybody. I only know, and I have already stated that, that the leading people in state, public, and other institutions who were not Serbs lost their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dzafic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender these two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same objection. The same objection. There is a bucket missing here, there is water missing there, there is a signature missing here, there is a stamp missing there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it goes to the weight. The witness has already spoken about the document 00849A. We can also see on the document that preceded the first document, which has the Broj number 117, it does have a stamp, it does -- it appears to have a signature on the document, and I would -- I'm sorry, Mr. Tieger wants to add something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would just add, Mr. President, that this -- these documents have indeed been authenticated. Now we've gone a step farther to show that they're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You said it has been authenticated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I understand that the ultimate determination of that is in the Court's hands. But I'm saying that the earmarks and indicia of authenticity have been provided with regard to stamps, with regard to sequence, and the order, and so on. Now the accused raises some speculation about what might have happened with these documents, which is entirely baseless and of the type that could be advanced on an imaginative basis for virtually every document that's been tendered by the Defence in this case. There's no basis for ignoring the classic earmarks of authenticity that exist with respect to these documents and that have been amplified by the additional document that has been proffered, and, as Ms. Sutherland has noted, to the extent that the speculation of the accused is ultimately given any weight by the Court, that goes to the weight of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But it's true that in dealing with scope of such --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm addressing the parties. I'll be very brief. But in conducting a trial of this size, it's true -- and also it has been our practice not to challenge the authenticity with such a seriousness. But there is a specific challenge from a party, the thing may be different. We'll mark these two documents for identification and come back to this issue very soon in due course after the deliberation on the part of the Chamber. Is there anything further to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I have no further questions for the witness. And I would just let Your Honours know that 65 ter number 00920 and 16080, the English translations have now been uploaded. And also the last document, 65 ter number 00874, which was the document that wasn't in full, has now been uploaded into e-court and that has the names of 1,163 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We've passed the time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly, please. We would not challenge the authenticity. However, it is obvious that there is a stamp, but I can't see Jovo Banjac, but this was sent to all the companies. How come that the complete document was not found in any of the companies? I believe that this was falsified after the Bosnian army entered Kljuc. If this was sent to all the companies together with a signature and the stamp, I'm sure that it should have been found in its complete form somewhere, in some of those companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need expert advice from Mr. Robinson. I don't follow Mr. Karadzic when he said he does not challenge the authenticity, while he's saying, raising the possibility of falsification. We will come to this issue later on. We will give the number for these two documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 849A shall be assigned Exhibit P3516, and 65 ter document 848 shall be assigned Exhibit P3517, both marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dzafic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for giving it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [In English] Excellencies, I said we would not. We would not. This is matter of translation. We would not contest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will come back to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will resume on Monday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of October, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.35 p.m.,
